scope: Bounded C3GN map: alternative complement pathway dysregulation, acquired convertase stabilization, complement-regulatory variants and glomerular complement deposition. Dense deposit disease is excluded as a phenotype; mixed C3 glomerulopathy studies are labelled and cannot establish C3GN-specific effects. Infection-related and immune-complex glomerulonephritis are excluded.

paragraphs.text: Glomerular proteomics identified alternative-pathway and terminal-complement proteins in the C3GN case series. Most patients with native kidney disease had stable renal function during reported follow-up, qualifying an inevitable progressive-failure interpretation. Patient nephritic-factor IgG stabilized alternative-pathway C3 convertase in biochemical assays.

These selected findings describe a bounded candidate, whose overall explanation has not been independently checked against current literature. Deposited proteins do not by themselves prove the sequence or sufficiency of injury mechanisms. Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending. Treatment efficacy has not been synthesized in this summary.
